# Refunds and Uncovered Matters
Fenwray Film Society is a fictional organisation.

Adopted: 25 March 2025
Effective: 1 April 2025

## 1. Member ticket cancellations
1.1 A ticket holder may request cancellation in writing.
1.2 Requests received at least 48 hours before the screening receive a full refund.
1.3 Requests received later receive no refund.
1.4 The receipt time recorded by the secretary decides which rule applies.
1.5 Refunds are made within 10 working days of approval.

## 2. Society screening cancellations
2.1 If the society cancels a screening, every paid ticket receives a full refund.
2.2 If the advertised film changes, buyers may request a full refund before entry.
2.3 A buyer who enters after being informed of the change loses that option.
2.4 No additional travel or accommodation expenses are reimbursed.

## 3. Equipment booking cancellations
3.1 A borrower may cancel by writing to the equipment officer.
3.2 Cancellation at least seven calendar days before collection receives a full hire-fee refund.
3.3 Cancellation later than that receives 50% of the hire fee.
3.4 The cancellation receipt date determines the applicable refund.
3.5 Security deposits are returned in full when collection never occurred.
3.6 Damage and late-return deductions follow film-equipment.md.

## 4. Refund administration
4.1 Refunds are issued by bank transfer unless cash repayment is agreed.
4.2 Refund requests must identify the booking or ticket concerned.
4.3 The treasurer keeps a record of the amount, reason and payment date.
4.4 Membership fee refunds are governed by film-fees.md.

## 5. Matters not covered
5.1 These rules do not establish a hardship or emergency-membership scheme.
5.2 They do not set compensation for lost personal property.
5.3 They do not specify film selection or programming criteria.
5.4 The committee considers these matters individually if they arise.
5.5 Individual decisions do not automatically create a continuing policy.

# Fees and Payments
Fenwray Film Society is a fictional organisation.

1.4 The membership period is determined by film-membership.md.

2.1 Standard admission costs £7 per screening.
2.2 Members with active membership pay £4 per screening.
2.3 Children aged under 12 pay £3 when accompanied by an adult.
2.4 Children aged 12 to 15 pay £5.
2.5 A member cannot buy discounted tickets for non-members.

3.2 Screen hire costs £8 per booking day.

# Volunteer Front-Desk Quick Guide
Fenwray Film Society is a fictional organisation.

Prepared: 8 April 2025
Last reviewed: 15 July 2025

This sheet is for quick answers, not formal decisions.
The governing documents prevail over this summary.
Check film-changes.md for later decisions before quoting a figure.

## 1. Joining the society
1.1 People aged 16 and over can apply.
1.2 Under-18s need a parent or guardian's written agreement.
1.3 Adults pay roughly £25 to £30 annually.
1.4 Younger members pay £12 annually.
1.5 Membership usually runs to the end of February.
1.6 Ask the secretary if someone has recently renewed.

## 2. Coming to a film
2.1 Public screenings are normally held twice monthly.
2.2 Standard admission is £7.
2.3 Members usually pay around £4 or £5.
2.4 Children have lower prices depending on age.
2.5 Reservations open about two weeks before the film.
2.6 Seats are limited, so advance payment is recommended.

## 3. Borrowing the equipment
3.1 Adult members may borrow the projector or screen.
3.2 Bookings need a few days' notice.
3.3 The projector costs £18 per day and the screen £8.
3.4 Taking both together costs £23 per day.
3.5 Expect a refundable deposit of around £80 to £100.
3.6 The usual loan is a few days, subject to the current limit.

## 4. Cancellations and problems
4.1 Early ticket cancellation normally qualifies for a refund.
4.2 Equipment cancellation may result in a partial charge.
4.3 The society refunds tickets when it cancels a screening.
4.4 Report faulty equipment promptly to the equipment officer.

## 5. Before giving a definite answer
5.1 Check the relevant governing document and changes register.
5.2 Do not promise an exception without committee authority.

content.text:
**No. Under the rules, you aren't entitled to the £4 back.**

- **The rule that applies:** film-refunds.md §2.2 says that if the advertised film changes, buyers may request a full refund *before entry*. You were told about the replacement at the door, so you had that option.
- **Why you lost it:** §2.3 says a buyer who enters after being informed of the change loses that option. You went in knowing about the change, so the refund right ended there.
- **Leaving after 20 minutes:** Nothing in the rules gives a refund for leaving early or for not liking the film.
- **Other refund routes:** The 48-hour cancellation rule (§1.2) doesn't help, because you didn't cancel in advance. The society also didn't cancel the screening (§2.1), because it only swapped the film.
- **Dates:** I checked the changes register (film-changes.md). The later amendments (the £5 member price from Feb 2026 and the 72-hour notice from Sept 2026) don't affect a 15 May 2025 screening, and the refund rules were already in force from 1 April 2025.

The rules don't give you a right to a refund, but you could still ask the committee for a goodwill refund. The quick guide says front-desk volunteers can't promise exceptions without committee authority. Any such decision would be a one-off and wouldn't set a policy (§5.5). If you ask, say you'd have wanted to claim a refund at the door but were already inside. That doesn't change the rules, but it's the fairest framing of your case.
